answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making voting weight grow only through a long, uniquely signed work trail. Picture a willow that thickens after many seasons: each new identity starts nearly weightless until independent reviewers, looking through a shared prism of blinded work samples, confirm the labor is not a cloned farm. A sudden swarm of lookalike accounts cannot reproduce the historical signal of consistent, non-transferable effort, so cheap mass identities stay thin and cannot swing consensus.
